landing.honestyTitle: What is real and what is not

honesty.simulated: This is a demonstration. Centres, weekly reports, child counts and estimates are simulated for Gicumbi and clearly labelled "simulated data" wherever they appear.
honesty.real: District and sector boundaries are real public data (NISR via geoBoundaries). The stunting figure for Gicumbi is the published RDHS 2025 value; sector values around it are simulated.
honesty.phase2: Phase 2 loads the Census, EICV7, DHS, Labour Force Survey, education statistics and NCDA's register into the same structures.
honesty.privacy: No child names, photos or IDs are ever collected. Parent locations are rounded to a 500 m square.

methodology.title: How it works
methodology.lead: The full data process, from sources to the decision a person takes, and what is real today versus simulated.

sources.title: Sources
sources.what: Official statistics, public maps and partner registers.
sources.today: Real boundaries; everything else simulated for Gicumbi.
sources.phase2: Census 2022, EICV7, DHS 2025, LFS 2025, education yearbook, NCDA register, WorldPop, OpenStreetMap.

alignment.title: Alignment
alignment.what: Every source is matched to sectors with its year, origin and checks.
alignment.today: The demo generator writes the same tables with origin = simulated.
alignment.phase2: One adapter per source, with checks that must pass before loading.

models.title: Models
models.what: Need per sector with ranges, coverage within walking distance, early warning.
models.today: Explainable baselines: stored estimates, straight-line catchments, rules against each centre's own history.
models.phase2: Small-area estimation calibrated to official totals, walking-time catchments, anomaly detection.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.what: A ranked shortlist within the budget, with reasons, ranges and sources.
suggestions.today: Greedy maximal coverage with your policy weights; compared with a largest-population-first baseline.
suggestions.phase2: An exact optimisation model behind the same screen.

decision.title: Human decision
decision.what: Approve, edit or reject. Rejections need a reason.
decision.today: Fully working, with an audit log that cannot be edited.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.what: Weekly reports, parent requests and rejection reasons shape the next round.
feedback.today: Rejections become constraints; parent requests raise a site's value; reports drive alerts.
feedback.phase2: Models retrained on what decisions and reports show.

plan.failed: The plan could not be run. Try again.

plan.methodText: Each round picks the action with the most weighted benefit per franc that still fits the budget, counting only children within a {minutes}-minute walk who do not yet have a place. Rejected sites are excluded and hard-to-reach sites count half. Method: {version}. Phase 2 replaces it with an exact optimisation model.

national.lead: All 30 districts at district level, with ranges. Sector detail and planning are open for your own district.

national.note: The CSV export gives district aggregates only; counts below 5 are written as <5 and every row states its origin.

tour.title: Five-minute tour
tour.lead: A guided walk through the pitch. Each step opens the right page, signs in as the demo planner when needed, and points at what to look at. It runs entirely on the seeded demo data.
tour.label: Guided tour
tour.offline: The tour needs no internet connection: every step uses the local demo database. If the map basemap cannot load, maps show the boundaries only.

welcome.title: The problem
welcome.text: Pre-primary enrolment must nearly double by 2029, and stunting in Gicumbi stands at 38.8%. Districts must decide where to invest, with uneven data.
welcome.say: Say: the map shows what exists. IrereroAI shows what to do next.

needMap.title: Need, with honest ranges
needMap.text: Gicumbi's sectors coloured by need. Hatched sectors have the least certain estimates. Red dots are centres that are overcrowded or have no water; rings are parent requests.
needMap.say: Say: we show uncertainty instead of hiding it. Everything here is labelled simulated.

reject.title: Suggest, then decide
reject.text: Press "Get suggestions". Cyumba village site A ranks high because parents asked for a centre there. Reject it with "No land available" and watch the list refill without it.
reject.say: Say: the rejection reason becomes a rule for every later plan, and it is in the audit log.

whatIf.title: Our plan against population alone
whatIf.text: Compare up to three budgets and weightings with placing centres where the most children live. The plan reaches more high-risk children for the same money.
whatIf.say: Say: these are children and mothers reached, never a predicted fall in stunting.

parent.title: A parent asks for a centre
parent.text: In Cyumba the nearest centre is a long walk away. Press "Request a centre here". Only a 500 m square is stored, with no name or phone number.
parent.say: Say: requests appear on the planner's map and raise the value of sites near them.

promise.title: Our promise
promise.text: AI suggests, people decide. Every suggestion has reasons, a range and its sources; nothing happens automatically; and every number on screen says whether it is real or simulated.
promise.say: Say: Phase 2 loads the real Census, DHS, EICV and NCDA data into the same structures.
